newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to tender for 18,000t corn/12,000t soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for 18,000t corn/12,000t soybeans.

text.p: Taiwan is expected to tender for 18,000 tonnes of corn and 12,000 tonnes of soybeans next week, traders said on Friday.
The state-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp will probably tender for a combined shipment of 18,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. corn and 12,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. soybeans, the dealers said.
The delivery date for the shipment from the U.S. Gulf of Mexico is from November 1-15 or from the Pacific Northwest from November 15-30, they added.
Taiwan's FGEP corn buying group is also expected to retender within three weeks for a 54,000 tonne-cargo of U.S. corn.
The delivery date will be from from December 10-25 from the Gulf or December 26-January 9 from the Pacific Northwest.

Buyers said pressure from the U.S. corn harvest season could push Chicago prices to test a floor at US$2.70 a bushel. The December futures corn contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) closed on Thursday 3-3/4 cents down at $2.90 a bushel.
"Corn will remain bearish in the harvest season," an executive at Taiwan's Formosa Oilseeds said.
"The FGEP group passed on its 54,000 tonne corn tender on October 9 due to buyers' bearish views," a corn buyer said.
The buyer added that the group may wait up to two weeks before retendering the shipment.
The Taiwan Flour Mills Association will probably remain sidelined next week after recently buying 60,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, traders said.
Domestic soymeal prices were quoted at between T$9.70-$9.90 a kg on Friday for Taipei delivery, down from $9.80-$10.00 a week earlier.
Corn powder was quoted at T$7.12 a kg for Taipei delivery, down from T$7.17 last week, dealers said.

Freight rates between the U.S. Pacific Northwestand Taiwan were quoted at about $11.00 a tonne and from the Gulf of Mexico at between $18.50-$19.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized November and December shipments.
Local wheat flour was quoted at T$14.55-$15.68 a kg, unchanged from last week, dealers said.
